evidence: src/infrastructure/config/container.ts: buildControllers() is the composition root. Its doc comment says it is 'the single place where abstractions are bound to implementations'.
src/infrastructure/config/container.ts: seedCatalogue(products) is called inside buildControllers(), right after InMemoryProductRepository is created, so seeding is part of the bootstrap step.
src/infrastructure/config/seedCatalogue.ts: seedCatalogue(products: ProductRepository) takes the repository interface, not the concrete InMemoryProductRepository.
src/infrastructure/config/seedCatalogue.ts: entities are built with Product.create({...}) and Money.ofCents(...), so domain invariants are not bypassed or copied.
src/infrastructure/config/container.ts: shared dependencies (lookup, allocations, reservation, clock) are each created once and reused, so no wiring is duplicated.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files in src/infrastructure/config deal with application bootstrap. container.ts is the composition root: buildControllers() creates the repositories, clock, ID generator and services, then passes them to the use cases and controllers. seedCatalogue.ts fills the product repository with starting data, and it is called only from that composition root. Seeding the initial data is part of the startup wiring, so the module has one clear purpose. seedCatalogue goes through the module's own abstractions: it takes the ProductRepository interface rather than the in-memory class, and it builds entities with Product.create and Money.ofCents instead of constructing them by hand. No rule or invariant is duplicated. Prices and stock levels are stored once as plain data in CATALOGUE, and all validation stays in the domain factories. container.ts also creates each shared dependency only once (lookup, allocations, reservation, clock) and reuses it everywhere.
